name: Flight of the Falcon

waypoints.name: Squire Creek Road Trailhead
waypoints.note: Access from Darrington via Squire Creek Road to blocked parking; road washed out ~2 mi in.
waypoints.directions: From Seattle, take I-5 north to the Arlington exit and follow SR 530 east through Oso to Darrington. Turn south on Madison Avenue to the T, go right on Darrington Street, and follow it as it becomes Squire Creek Road at the west end of town. Drive to the end of the road, about 1,100 feet, where a washout roughly two miles in gates it and blocks the parking area. Park at the gate; the old roadbed beyond it is walking only.

waypoints.name: Waterfall Basin (base of walls)
waypoints.note: ~3-3.5 hr to the basin and the base of Roan Wall via old roadbed, streambed, and a Squire Creek ford, below Three Fingers' east face. Salish Peak's base is farther on, up the left side of Roan Wall.
waypoints.directions: Walk the old roadbed past a flagged landslide crossing and the original road end to a wide, dry streambed of white boulders. Descend the bed about 200 ft, trend left into the alders to find the informal path, and follow it to the ford of Squire Creek, then on as the trail fades until the basin opens. Scramble the thin boulder-filled watercourse that comes down from the wall to the base beside Martha's Place, the huge overhung boulder.

approach: From Seattle, drive I-5 north to the Arlington exit, then SR 530 east through Oso to Darrington, and turn onto Squire Creek Road at the west end of town, following it to the parking area where it's gated off by washout damage. From there the approach is long and rough: hike the old roadbed past a landslide crossing (~5 minutes in), reach the original road end around 30-40 minutes from the car, then follow a faint trail through a dry streambed and alder brush, ford Squire Creek, and pick through obscure forest track before finally breaking out into the open basin roughly 2 hours from the car. This is a known bushwhacky, unmaintained approach typical of Darrington-area crags, with route-finding (flagging, cairns) required in several spots.
